answer: Divergent-Reply Challenge. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge by deriving a unique response from its private key and the challenge; honest agents produce distinct answers per challenge. Because clones share identical state, they emit identical replies, colliding on a shared transcript. Registries reject any duplicate response as a sybil signal, so an attacker must acquire genuinely independent keys per clone, each with its own costly setup (a falcon signing keypair and provisioning). A cheap ivory token can't fake divergence, exposing the fable of free multiplicity.
